previous_statement: Finite-polyhedron presentation. Choose a homeomorphism h from breve-calU onto a finite simplicial complex K supplied by lem-stage1-bound-quotient-index-data, regard K as its finite polyhedron, and conjugate breve-sigma to f=h o breve-sigma o h^{-1}:K->K. Under the singleton hypothesis Fix(f)={h(breve-e)}; lem-finite-polyhedron-maximal-simplex-placement puts h(breve-e) in a maximal simplex. Cohomological naturality under h gives L(f)=L(breve-sigma), and the local fixed-point index is invariant under this conjugate presentation, so ind(f,h(breve-e))=ind(breve-sigma,breve-e)=+1.
new_statement: Finite-polyhedron presentation without conjugating the map. Let h:breve-calU->|K| be the homeomorphism to the realization of a finite simplicial complex supplied by lem-stage1-bound-quotient-index-data, and transport the finite-polyhedron structure of |K| along h to the same underlying topological space breve-calU. Denote this finite-polyhedron presentation by X, and let f:X->X be the same underlying function breve-sigma (not h o breve-sigma o h^{-1}). Under the singleton hypothesis Fix(f)={breve-e}; node 1.6 (using lem-finite-polyhedron-maximal-simplex-placement) places breve-e in a maximal simplex of this presentation. Because X and breve-calU have the same underlying space and f and breve-sigma are literally the same self-map, the local index occurring in lem-topology-lefschetz-hopf is exactly ind(f,breve-e)=ind(breve-sigma,breve-e)=+1 as supplied by lem-stage1-bound-quotient-index-data, and f^{*k}=breve-sigma^{*k} on the same cohomology groups, hence L(f)=L(breve-sigma). No invariance of index under homeomorphic conjugacy is used.
